html:
Operation Storm was a Croatian army offensive from 4 to 7 August 1995 that retook the Krajina, the area held by rebel Serbs since 1991, and its capital Knin.

Croatia had rebuilt its army while a United Nations ceasefire held. The rebel force collapsed within days. About 150,000 to 200,000 Serbs fled to Bosnia and Serbia, one of the largest single flights of the Yugoslav wars, and many who stayed behind were killed or saw their homes burned. The offensive also relieved the besieged Bosnian town of Bihać and helped force the Bosnian Serbs to the Dayton talks. Croats celebrate it as Victory Day; Serbs remember it as an exodus.
sum: Operation Storm was a Croatian army offensive from 4 to 7 August 1995 that retook the Krajina, the area held by rebel Serbs since 1991, and its capital Knin.
